exercises.translation: Describe a red book, without changing the supplied adjective's tense. Use 赤い (あかい); put only the adjective and any required linker in the blank.
exercises.evidence: The head noun is already printed. This is an ordinary affirmative nonpast i-adjective description.
exercises.explanation: 赤い attaches directly to 本. The main sentence's polite です stays after the whole noun phrase.

options.label: 赤い
options.rationale: The i-adjective attaches directly to the noun.

options.label: 赤いな
options.rationale: Adding な after this i-adjective does not form the requested description.

exercises.translation: Describe a spacious room, without changing the supplied adjective's tense. Use 広い (ひろい); put only the adjective and any required linker in the blank.
exercises.evidence: The head noun is already printed. This is an ordinary affirmative nonpast i-adjective description.
exercises.explanation: 広い attaches directly to 部屋. The main sentence's polite です stays after the whole noun phrase.

options.label: 広い
options.rationale: The i-adjective attaches directly to the noun.

options.label: 広いな
options.rationale: Adding な after this i-adjective does not form the requested description.

exercises.translation: Describe the room as quiet in the past. Use the ordinary plain past of the na-adjective 静か (しずか) directly before the noun. Keep the printed main ending.
exercises.evidence: The requested past meaning belongs inside the noun description; the main identification remains これは...です.
exercises.explanation: 静かだった is the ordinary plain past description. Do not add な before だった. The sentence does not say the property has necessarily ceased.

options.label: 静かなだった
options.rationale: This incorrectly keeps the affirmative nonpast な link before だった.

options.label: 静かだった
options.rationale: The plain past adjective predicate modifies the head noun.

exercises.translation: Describe the station as lively in the past. Use the ordinary plain past of the na-adjective にぎやか (にぎやか) directly before the noun. Keep the printed main ending.
exercises.evidence: The requested past meaning belongs inside the noun description; the main identification remains これは...です.
exercises.explanation: にぎやかだった is the ordinary plain past description. Do not add な before だった. The sentence does not say the property has necessarily ceased.

options.label: にぎやかなだった
options.rationale: This incorrectly keeps the affirmative nonpast な link before だった.

options.label: にぎやかだった
options.rationale: The plain past adjective predicate modifies the head noun.

exercises.translation: This is the book I read yesterday. Convert 読みました (よみました) to its ordinary uncontracted plain modifier form, keeping the stated tense/aspect and verb. Do not add a nominalizer.
exercises.evidence: The head noun is stated after the blank; the main polite identification is already complete.
exercises.explanation: 読みました becomes 読んだ before the noun. The plain past describes the completed event, not a past main identification. No linking の is added after this plain verb.

options.label: 読んだ
options.rationale: This keeps the supplied completed-event meaning in a plain modifier.

options.label: 読んでいる
options.rationale: This changes the description to te-iru rather than preserving the supplied past form.

options.label: 読んだの
options.rationale: An extra の does not link this ordinary verb clause to the stated head noun.

exercises.translation: This is the plate I washed yesterday. Convert 洗いました (あらいました) to its ordinary uncontracted plain modifier form, keeping the stated tense/aspect and verb. Do not add a nominalizer.
exercises.evidence: The head noun is stated after the blank; the main polite identification is already complete.
exercises.explanation: 洗いました becomes 洗った before the noun. The plain past describes the completed event, not a past main identification. No linking の is added after this plain verb.

options.label: 洗った
options.rationale: This keeps the supplied completed-event meaning in a plain modifier.

options.label: 洗っている
options.rationale: This changes the description to te-iru rather than preserving the supplied past form.

options.label: 洗ったの
options.rationale: An extra の does not link this ordinary verb clause to the stated head noun.

exercises.explanation: 読んでいます becomes 読んでいる before the noun. The te-iru description preserves the ongoing event in this scene. No linking の is added after this plain verb.

options.label: 読んだ
options.rationale: A plain past modifier describes the completed event; it does not preserve the requested ongoing reading.

options.label: 読んでいる
options.rationale: This keeps the supplied ongoing te-iru description.

options.label: 読んでいるの
options.rationale: An extra の does not link this ordinary verb clause to the stated head noun.

exercises.translation: This is the plate my mother is washing. Convert 洗っています (あらっています) to its ordinary uncontracted plain modifier form, keeping the stated tense/aspect and verb. Do not add a nominalizer.
exercises.evidence: The head noun is stated after the blank; the main polite identification is already complete.
exercises.explanation: 洗っています becomes 洗っている before the noun. The te-iru description preserves the ongoing event in this scene. No linking の is added after this plain verb.

exercises.translation: This is a house with a garden. Turn あります (exists/is present) into an ordinary affirmative nonpast plain noun description, and include the subject marker が before the verb. Do not change the supplied nouns.
exercises.evidence: The feature noun is printed before the blank, and the head noun after it; both the case marker and the plain verb are needed.
exercises.explanation: 庭がある describes 家. In this sentence the whole phrase is identified with です; in another sentence it could take を or another particle.

options.label: があった
options.rationale: This describes a past feature, not the requested nonpast description.

options.label: があります
options.rationale: The requested ordinary modifier uses plain ある, not the supplied polite main-clause form.

options.label: がある
options.rationale: This marks the feature with が and places plain ある before the head noun.

exercises.translation: This is a room with a window. Turn あります (exists/is present) into an ordinary affirmative nonpast plain noun description, and include the subject marker が before the verb. Do not change the supplied nouns.
exercises.evidence: The feature noun is printed before the blank, and the head noun after it; both the case marker and the plain verb are needed.
exercises.explanation: 窓がある describes 部屋. In this sentence the whole phrase is identified with です; in another sentence it could take を or another particle.

options.label: があった
options.rationale: This describes a past feature, not the requested nonpast description.

options.label: があります
options.rationale: The requested ordinary modifier uses plain ある, not the supplied polite main-clause form.

exercises.prompt: これは私の傘です。あれは____です。
exercises.translation: These are two umbrellas. 'This is mine; that one is my older sister’s'. Build the possessive phrase from 姉 (あね), leaving the already identified item unspoken. Do not repeat its noun or replace the owner with a pronoun.
exercises.evidence: The same kind of item is explicit in the first sentence; the blank needs the owner plus possessive の.
exercises.explanation: 姉の refers to the owner's understood 傘. This is not nominalization of an activity or explanatory の.

options.label: 姉の
options.rationale: The owner plus の identifies the understood item.

options.label: 姉
options.rationale: This identifies the distant item as the owner, rather than as that person's possession.

options.label: 姉なの
options.rationale: This is not the requested ordinary possessive noun phrase.

exercises.prompt: これは私の鍵です。あれは____です。
exercises.translation: These are two keys. 'This is mine; that one is the teacher’s'. Build the possessive phrase from 先生 (せんせい), leaving the already identified item unspoken. Do not repeat its noun or replace the owner with a pronoun.
exercises.evidence: The same kind of item is explicit in the first sentence; the blank needs the owner plus possessive の.
exercises.explanation: 先生の refers to the owner's understood 鍵. This is not nominalization of an activity or explanatory の.

options.label: 先生の
options.rationale: The owner plus の identifies the understood item.

options.label: 先生
options.rationale: This identifies the distant item as the owner, rather than as that person's possession.

options.label: 先生なの
options.rationale: This is not the requested ordinary possessive noun phrase.

exercises.translation: Choosing among already identified items, ask for the red one. Build the ordinary affirmative nonpast 'the ... one' phrase with 赤い (あかい) and の; do not repeat a noun or substitute another adjective.
exercises.evidence: The blank contains the whole adjective-plus-の phrase; を belongs to the printed request.
exercises.explanation: An i-adjective attaches directly to the substitute の, without な. The whole item phrase takes を here; の is not restricted to a following は or が.

options.label: 赤いだの
options.rationale: だの is not the requested ordinary adjective-plus-の item phrase.

options.label: 赤いの
options.rationale: Direct の attachment fits this i-adjective.

options.label: 赤いなの
options.rationale: This incorrectly adds な to the supplied i-adjective.

exercises.translation: Choosing among already identified items, ask for the large one. Build the ordinary affirmative nonpast 'the ... one' phrase with 大きい (おおきい) and の; do not repeat a noun or substitute another adjective.
exercises.evidence: The blank contains the whole adjective-plus-の phrase; を belongs to the printed request.
exercises.explanation: An i-adjective attaches directly to the substitute の, without な. The whole item phrase takes を here; の is not restricted to a following は or が.

options.label: 大きいだの
options.rationale: だの is not the requested ordinary adjective-plus-の item phrase.

options.label: 大きいの
options.rationale: Direct の attachment fits this i-adjective.

options.label: 大きいなの
options.rationale: This incorrectly adds な to the supplied i-adjective.

exercises.translation: Choosing among already identified rooms, ask for the quiet one. Build the ordinary affirmative nonpast 'the ... one' phrase with 静か (しずか) and の; do not repeat a noun or substitute another adjective.

options.label: 静かだの

options.label: 静かの
options.rationale: This omits the needed な in this ordinary na-adjective pattern.

options.label: 静かなの
options.rationale: な correctly links this na-adjective to the substitute の.

exercises.translation: Choosing among already identified rooms, ask for the clean one. Build the ordinary affirmative nonpast 'the ... one' phrase with きれい (きれい) and の; do not repeat a noun or substitute another adjective.

exercises.translation: I like reading books. Convert 読みます (よみます) to the ordinary nonpast plain verb and nominalize it with の. Preserve the printed object, が and final predicate; do not substitute こと.
exercises.evidence: The blank needs the verb as well as the nominalizer; を is already attached to the inner object and が follows the whole activity.
exercises.explanation: 読むの turns the activity into the noun-like phrase evaluated by 好き. The printed 本を remains the object of 読む. The named の formation is the exercise goal, not a claim that こと or topic/contrast markers never occur in related sentences.

options.label: 読むの
options.rationale: Plain nonpast verb plus の supplies the requested activity phrase.

options.label: 読む
options.rationale: The verb alone leaves the presented activity-nominalization pattern incomplete.

exercises.prompt: 私は本____読むのが好きです。
exercises.translation: Use the same ordinary activity statement: like reading books. Insert the case marker for the thing read inside the activity. Preserve the subject/topic, plain active verb and outer のが; do not change to a topic, contrast or passive construction.
exercises.evidence: The blank is inside 読む's clause, not between the completed activity and 好き.
exercises.explanation: 本を読む names the activity with its own object. The outer のが belongs to the preference/skill construction, not to that inner object. English 'like' and 'be good at' do not determine every Japanese particle in the sentence.

options.label: が
options.rationale: Here が would make this inner noun the verb's subject instead of preserving the stated thing acted on.

options.label: を
options.rationale: を preserves the transitive verb's inner object; the printed のが then marks the whole activity.

options.label: 洗う

exercises.prompt: 作った料理を食べました。→____
exercises.translation: I ate the food I made. What is marked by the を immediately before 食べました: the food itself, or the activity of making food? Answer with 物 (もの, the physical item) or 活動 (かつどう, the activity); these are response labels, not definitions of every use of those words.
exercises.evidence: Read the head noun or the nominalized clause, and the role assigned to that whole phrase by the following predicate.
exercises.explanation: The preceding past clause describes the head noun; the thing eaten/shown is that noun's referent, not the preceding action.

options.label: 物
options.rationale: This identifies the actual item described by the clause.

options.label: 活動
options.rationale: 作った describes 料理, and を marks that food as what was eaten. The activity of making it is not what was eaten.

exercises.prompt: 料理を作るのが好きです。→____
exercises.translation: I like preparing food. What is evaluated by 好き: the food itself, or the activity of making food? Answer with 物 (もの, the physical item) or 活動 (かつどう, the activity); these are response labels, not definitions of every use of those words.
exercises.evidence: Read the head noun or the nominalized clause, and the role assigned to that whole phrase by the following predicate.
exercises.explanation: The inner noun is acted on by the verb, but the whole verb clause plus の is what 好き evaluates.

options.label: 物
options.rationale: 料理 is the object inside 作る's clause; 好き evaluates the whole 料理を作るの activity, not the food itself.

options.label: 活動
options.rationale: This identifies the entire nominalized activity rather than its inner object.

options.label: 活動

exercises.prompt: 写真を撮るのが好きです。→____

exercises.evidence: Read the head noun or the nominalized clause, and the role assigned to that whole phrase by the following predicate.
exercises.explanation: The inner noun is acted on by the verb, but the whole verb clause plus の is what 好き evaluates.

options.label: 物
options.rationale: 写真 is the object inside 撮る's clause; 好き evaluates the whole 写真を撮るの activity, not the photograph itself.

options.label: 活動
options.rationale: This identifies the entire nominalized activity rather than its inner object.

exercises.translation: Meaning: 'bread my mother baked'. Can the displayed subject が be replaced by の in this same ordinary structure, keeping the same subject and meaning? Choose できる (replacement works here) or できない (not as the same subject-marking construction). Do not invent an omitted possessed noun, explanatory ending or different sentence.
exercises.evidence: These are either simple clauses before a stated head noun, or ordinary independent clauses.
exercises.explanation: Subject の is possible in this simple noun modifier: 母の焼いたパン. It is not a rule permitting every が in every longer modifier to change.

options.label: できる
options.rationale: The subject is inside one of the simple noun-modifying patterns taught here.

options.label: できない
options.rationale: This wrongly rejects the licensed subject の in this simple modifier.

exercises.translation: Meaning: 'a day when it rained'. Can the displayed subject が be replaced by の in this same ordinary structure, keeping the same subject and meaning? Choose できる (replacement works here) or できない (not as the same subject-marking construction). Do not invent an omitted possessed noun, explanatory ending or different sentence.
exercises.evidence: These are either simple clauses before a stated head noun, or ordinary independent clauses.
exercises.explanation: Subject の is possible in this simple noun modifier: 雨の降った日. It is not a rule permitting every が in every longer modifier to change.

options.label: できる
options.rationale: The subject is inside one of the simple noun-modifying patterns taught here.

options.label: できない
options.rationale: This wrongly rejects the licensed subject の in this simple modifier.

exercises.prompt: 母がパンを焼きました。→____
exercises.translation: Meaning: 'Mother baked bread.'. Can the displayed subject が be replaced by の in this same ordinary structure, keeping the same subject and meaning? Choose できる (replacement works here) or できない (not as the same subject-marking construction). Do not invent an omitted possessed noun, explanatory ending or different sentence.
exercises.evidence: These are either simple clauses before a stated head noun, or ordinary independent clauses.
exercises.explanation: This が marks the subject of the independent clause. の is not a drop-in replacement preserving that role; other constructions with の are a different question.

options.label: できる
options.rationale: There is no following head noun to make this the taught subject の modifier pattern.

options.label: できない
options.rationale: Keep が as the independent clause's subject marker in this ordinary statement.
